intro.title: Build typed monorepo package boundary checks
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple TypeScript tool that checks if code is correctly importing from allowed packages within a monorepo. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's type system to enforce boundaries between different packages, preventing unauthorized imports. The core concept involves creating a custom type guard and a validation function to analyze import statements. You'll work with key TypeScript constructs like interfaces, type aliases, and modules. By the end, you'll have a basic typed checker that helps maintain clean architecture in multi-package projects.
intro.usecase: In large-scale applications like enterprise dashboards or e-commerce platforms, monorepo package boundary checks ensure that components and utilities are only imported from approved packages, preventing dependency violations. For example, a dashboard's analytics module should not directly import internal payment processing utilities, maintaining clean separation between business domains. This pattern is crucial when building modular UI libraries where design system components must be isolated from business logic packages. Developers implement these checks to enforce architectural boundaries, similar to how a complex form builder prevents its validation logic from accessing unrelated data-fetching modules.
